openevolve_best_candidate.nature_of_edit: Genuine SELECTION change (matches this run's system_message steering toward tightening min_edge/min_confidence-style thresholds, not stake-size-only): raises min_edge 0.15->0.18, min_confidence 6.0->7.0, adds min_liquidity/max_price/min_combined(edge*confidence)/max_horizon_days filters that each independently drop trades, PLUS an adaptive stake multiplier (weighted by edge/confidence/price/horizon, capped <=1.5x base_stake) layered on top of (not instead of) the tightened selection. The fresh adversary independently verified the selection is a strict subset of baseline's own picks (23 vs 31), i.e. the improvement is driven by which trades are taken, not by uniformly leveraging the same trade set.

adversary_verdict.reason_verbatim: This is a genuine selection change, not leverage or variance amplification. My independent re-run of the diffed score_candidate against fixtures/pm_history.csv confirms the candidate's selection is a STRICT SUBSET of baseline's (23 picks vs 31) — its active filters (min_edge 0.15→0.18, min_confidence 6→7, new min_combined edge×confidence≥1.5, strict price ceiling 0.63) drop trades rather than resize the same set, so this changes WHICH bets are taken, exactly the mechanism the fixture generator documents as a true Pareto improvement (ALPHA=0.5 edge, corr(edge,outcome)≈+0.15). The three OOS test windows reproduce net = 4.920 / 5.358 / 2.375 (mean 4.218, std 1.315, ratio 3.208 — all matching the supplied pre-checks), and critically window 5 flips from baseline's LOSING −0.473 to +2.375 purely because the stricter filters eliminate the bad rows, so worst_window_oos_net_usd = 2.375 is positive and no hidden bad window is masked by the mean (EDGE-5 clear). std_oos (1.315) is not a near-zero artifact, the >3x trip-wire cleared, and the sizing multiplier is capped at ≤~1.1× (below baseline's flat 5.0), so the risk-adjusted gain cannot be a leverage trick. The code stays entirely inside the pure score_candidate function reading only its three plain-data args; several knobs (liquidity/max_price/max_horizon) are inert no-ops given the fixture ranges but harmless. The only residual caveat — window 1 selects just n=1 trade, making that window's net thin — is inherent to the 84-row fixture and offset by a principled, edge-aligned selection rule and a positive worst window, so I am willing to promote.
